clue.text: A Liberal preparing for war? That's disturbing

parts.note: a nation preparing for war is arming itself

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Liberal politician is gearing up for conflict, and finds the thought unsettling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alarming causes worry and unease, the same effect as a disturbing event.

clue.text: A vessel with fuel to discharge

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a vessel
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A ship carrying fuel is ready to unload.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discharge' suggests unloading cargo, but here it means to absolve or release from guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb for absolving or pardoning, freeing someone from sin or obligation.

clue.text: Woman writing article about soil improvement

indicators.note: the article goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: improving the soil works it over, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman writes an article on improving garden earth.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Raj lady beams when at sea with him

indicators.note: something at sea is confused and adrift, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A colonial lady smiles broadly when she is sailing with a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Under British rule in India (the Raj), this was the title for a European married woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian servants used this term of respect for a European woman during British colonial rule.

clue.text: This holds the clutch

parts.note: a clutch suggests a car pedal or a handbag, but it is a set of eggs laid together, held where birds sit

explanation.surface: Something that grips a car part or a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's home where eggs are laid and incubated is where a clutch of eggs sits.

clue.text: Fowl, weight of a pug

explanation.surface: A bird and the size of a small dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The pug here is a pugilist, a boxer, not the little dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A small breed of domestic chicken carries this name, and in boxing it is a light weight class for fighters.

clue.text: Jack accustomed to being vilified

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, and AB (able-bodied seaman) is a sailor
used to means accustomed to

explanation.surface: A sailor grown used to being insulted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vilified has been spoken about with insults and harsh criticism, treated with contempt.

clue.text: Edward's holding a number on a leash

indicators.note: Ted holds the anaesthetic inside his name

parts.note: Ted is a pet form of Edward; the possessive adds no letter
ether numbs, so it is a number, a thing that numbs

explanation.surface: Edward is holding a figure while walking his dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as a figure but means something that numbs, an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal tied with a rope or lead is restrained, tied up.

clue.text: Involving no harm, at strenuous event

indicators.note: strenuous suggests vigorous effort, so the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A tough race in which nobody comes to any harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-distance road race of about 26 miles is a sporting event.

clue.text: His smirk's potentially offensive

indicators.note: the letters could potentially form something else, so they are to be rearranged

parts.note: the possessive ending adds no letter; the word is taken as written

explanation.surface: A man's smug grin could give offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' reads as rude, but it is the noun: a military attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor clash between troops is a small-scale military attack, an offensive in miniature.

clue.text: Does it slice through the main?

definitions.text: Does it slice through the main?

parts.words: Does it slice through the main?
parts.note: read as a blade it slices things; 'the main' is the open sea, so it is also a vessel that cuts through the waves

explanation.surface: A question about something cutting through a pipe or main.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fast sailing vessel bears this name, as does any tool or person that cuts.

clue.text: Was in form when young

parts.note: being in form sounds like doing well, but a form is the resting place of a hare, and the animal here is a young one

explanation.surface: Someone who performed well in their youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby hare lives in a shallow hollow in grass called a form.

clue.text: I therefore stick line on the map

parts.note: so means therefore
a bar is a stick or rod

explanation.surface: Someone decides they will stick a pin on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather chart, a curve joining places of equal atmospheric pressure is drawn as a line.

clue.text: Belief held about folk in flats

indicators.note: the belief is held around the folk, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
men means people, folk

explanation.surface: A conviction shared by people living in apartments.
explanation.definitionFit: A large building divided into rented apartments, often in a city, is a block of flats.

clue.text: Heat bumps start to torment troops at scene of operations

indicators.note: the word heat is bumped about, its letters jumbled
the start of the word torment gives its first letter

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a body of troops

explanation.surface: Heat rash torments soldiers in a combat zone.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps; 'bumps' jumbles HEAT into THEA.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital operating room or a war zone is where operations take place.

clue.text: The girl's new form, after dieting?

indicators.note: the letters are given a new form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive ending adds no letter; the word is taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl shows off her slimmer figure after a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' pretends to be the girl's figure after slimming, but 'new form' signals the rearrangement; the definition rests on the dieter's weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has been dieting weighs less afterwards, so is less heavy.

clue.text: Do not allow duck to be held by its medico

parts.note: the duck's doctor is an animal doctor, a vet
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A vet refuses to let a duck be handled by anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbid or block a proposal is to exercise a right of refusal.

clue.text: The Spanish sheep getting hair clotted together

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
flocks are groups of sheep

explanation.surface: A Spanish flock of sheep with matted wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangled, matted locks of hair were said to be knotted by mischievous fairies.

clue.text: Suitable venue for the factory dance?

parts.note: works is a word for a factory
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A question about where to hold the staff party.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue suggests a staff party, but read in pieces it is a hop at the works.
explanation.definitionFit: A room where goods are made or repaired; a fitting place for the event the clue describes.

clue.text: Of conventional form, half-seen, covered by litter-container lid

parts.note: a sty holds a litter of pigs

indicators.note: the half word sits under the lid, inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: half of the word seen is wanted, so only its first two letters are kept

explanation.surface: Something barely visible under the lid of a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' suggests rubbish, but it is a litter of piglets, kept in a sty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stylised is shown in a conventional, simplified manner rather than realistically.

clue.text: See to return of rifle

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: a return turns the little word to back to front

explanation.surface: A soldier is told to attend to sending back a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like the gun, but it is the verb: to ransack or plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to search and steal from, which is what plundering or pillaging does.

clue.text: A chap embraced by mother becomes puce

indicators.note: the chap is hugged by mother, set inside her word

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a gent is a gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: A man hugged by his mother turns purple with embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are purplish-red colours, so one stands loosely as a synonym for the other.

clue.text: Free verse Welsh try to avoid

indicators.note: freeing the letters lets them move into a new order

explanation.surface: A Welsh poet attempts to dodge free verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn aside suddenly is to veer away from something to escape it.

clue.text: Vehicle, or a kit ordered for it

indicators.note: the letters are put in order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A vehicle, or a kit sent off for to build one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Russian carriage or sleigh drawn by three horses abreast.

clue.text: Bearing south-east, can't crash into it

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go into the compass abbreviation

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

indicators.note: a crash smashes the word into pieces, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored; the word is taken as written

explanation.surface: A ship heading south-east is unable to avoid running into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' suggests a compass direction, as the surface implies, but here it means posture.
explanation.definitionFit: One's bearing is one's posture or way of standing, an attitude of the body.

clue.text: Little enthusiasm for new mural circling botanical gardens

definitions.note: the definition is a noun phrase; the answer is the adjective describing it

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the gardens
the word mural is made new, its letters rearranged

parts.note: Kew Gardens in London is the famous Royal Botanic Gardens

explanation.surface: People feel lukewarm about a new mural surrounding a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London; it goes inside LUARM, the rearranged letters of mural.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-hearted, tepid feeling shows only a little keenness.

clue.text: Wine cartel of a kind

indicators.note: a cartel of a kind is a rough version of the word, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A wine-producing cartel of some sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Bordeaux is known in Britain by this name, a classic red wine.

clue.text: A mob overturning the pulpit

indicators.note: the mob turns things over, so its letters are upset into a new order

explanation.surface: A crowd knocks over the preacher's stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised reading desk or lectern in early churches, from which scripture was read.

clue.text: Fellow in the centre gets stick

indicators.note: the fellow is placed in the centre word

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
he stands for a male, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man in the middle is handed a cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' looks like a noun, a rod, but it is the verb: to cling together.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold together firmly is to adhere, just as things that stick do.

clue.text: Release me finally from assignment

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word me

parts.note: a mission is a task or assignment

explanation.surface: Someone begs to be let off a job at last.
explanation.definitionFit: A discharge or giving off of gas or light is a release into the surroundings.

clue.text: Meal for this consumer

explanation.surface: An evening meal for the person eating it.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening meal has this name; read as one who sups, it also means someone who drinks or eats.

clue.text: Plant forests? This takes time

parts.note: woods are forests
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Planting forests is a job that takes a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb applied to forests, but it is the noun being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A European wild herb of the mint family grows in woodland, a germander used as a flowering species.
